A history of underpinning. There is a history of underpinning to the property. It should be noted that different lenders may have different policies and approaches towards properties with history of underpinning. However, I did not note any visible signs of structural movement which indicates that any works have been functional so far. Your legal adviser should investigate and request the relevant documentation for the works that have been undertaken and ensure all remedial work is carried out under a long term and meaningful guarantee with a suitable insurance indemnity. It is imperative that the relevant documentation for this is requested to include Building Regulations approval.

We could not ascertain whether the building contains reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC). As the building is of concrete frame with concrete elements in various locations, including but not limited to the flooring, cladding and roof coverings, there is a possibility that this material may be present. We are not specialists and have not undertaken any intrusive investigations or specialist tests. You should make further enquiries with the building management as to whether any RAAC has been detected or if there is any information they may hold in their records, including any action plans, in regard to this matter. If RAAC has been or is identified, this is likely to have a large impact on the future saleability of the property and more importantly on the health and safety of the occupiers of the building.

No hazardous material was noted.

Lintel defect is present. Cracks to the front bay require Helifix bars and resin injection repairs. In addition, a crack to the front bay requires lintel repair.

Masonry bees were noted. There are holes in the external walls, typical of those produced by masonry bees, which can cause substantial erosion and weakness of the joints. The situation should be checked during the summer period when the bees are active and if these are seen entering the wall structure, the advice of the Environmental Health Officer of the Local Authority should be sought.
